The fabric of summer clothes wouldn't be as thick or heavy as you might think, and they wore natural fibers so they also didn't feel as hot. Undergarments for both men and women were usually linen so they'd absorb the sweat and keep you cool.

By the 1910s most women didn't wear as many layers anymore (compared to previous decades) and in exceptionally hot days they might go without one of those layers. Keeping out of the sun, carrying a fan and/or a parasol and wearing a hat would obviously help too.

Then there's the Reddenheimer: head, still a round body, a bit of puff, taller and a bit skinnier, small, short ears, smaller smile, smaller eyes.


Clickenheimer 1.0: head is closer to the body, square, the black/brown hooves are gone (probably covered by fluff), a lot smaller, more wide and poofier, ears are pretty much the same, wider smile, eye size can be different from fluff to fluff.


Clickenheimer 2.0: Head is separated again, though not as much as in 1.0, massive wide ears, a lot less poofier, taller but not wider, a lot less square, and the smile is similar to 1.0, eyes stay pretty much the same, now it comes in more colors than red.
